I don’t have access to your VirusTotal account so I can’t pull live data myself, but here’s exactly how you’d query the **sub‑domain** relationship for `example.org` and receive back only the identifiers (plus any optional “context” fields). --- ### 1️⃣ Build the HTTP Request | Element | Value | |---------|-------| | Base URL | `https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3` *(or `/api/v2` depending on the version you’re using)* | | Endpoint | `/objects/domains/{id}/relationships/subdomains` – replace `{id}` with the canonical ID of `example.org`, usually its SHA256 hash or simply the name itself (`example.org`). | | Query Parameters | `limit=10&continuation_cursor=abc` | | Headers |   - `x-apikey: my_api`
  - `Accept: application/json` | > **Example (curl)** > ```bash > curl -X GET \ > https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/objects/domains/example.org/relationships/subdomains?limit=10&continuation_cursor=abc \ > -H "x-apikey: my_api" > ``` --- ### 2️⃣ Expected JSON Response Structure ```json { "data": [ { "_links": { ... }, "attributes": {}, "id": "", "type": "object_descriptor", "relationship_type": "subdomain_of", "source_object_id": "" }, ... ], "meta": { "pagination": { "next_page_token": "...", "total_count": 42, "page_size": 10 } } } ``` *Only the `"id"` field (the unique identifier of each sub‑domain descriptor) and optionally any `"context_attributes"` you specify via the API parameters will appear.* If you wish to include additional context information—such as timestamps or source URLs—you can add those through the API's *fields* parameter: ```http GET …/relationships/subdomains?limit=10&continuation_cursor=abc&fields=context_attributes ``` --- ### 3️⃣ Things To Keep In Mind | Tip | Why It Matters | |-----|----------------| | **API Version** | VirusTotal has moved from V2 to V3 recently. Make sure you hit the correct base path (`v3`) unless you specifically need legacy features. | | **Rate Limits** | Each API key has limits per minute/hour/day. Exceeding them returns a `429 Too Many Requests`. | | **Pagination** | Even though you requested 10 items, there may still be more beyond the first page. Check the `next_page_token` under `meta.pagination`; pass it as `continuation_cursor=` for subsequent calls. | | **Error Handling** | A non‑200 status code means something went wrong. Inspect the body for error details. | --- #### Quick Checklist Before Running Your Call 1. Replace `` with `my_api`. 2. Confirm whether you’re targeting V2 or V3; adjust the base URL accordingly. 3. Verify that `example.org`’s canonical ID matches the one used in the endpoint. 4. Run the cURL command (or equivalent in Postman/Python/etc.) and capture the returned list of IDs. That’s everything you’ll need to programmatically obtain the sub‑domain descriptors while limiting the payload to just the IDs—and any extra context you explicitly request. Happy querying!
